raw_response:
I farm 7 mu, and I will not spread myself too thin. Wheat and maize are still my steady backbone, because I have well water and I know that land well. This year I will keep 3 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, 2 mu in cotton, and 2 mu in watermelon. That way I keep grain in the yard and still leave room for cash crops. I usually start from what I did last year and only push a little higher if I think the price and water can support it. With 40 years in the field, I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save a few yuan on fertilizer and lose yield, that hurts more than putting a bit extra. For wheat I will feed it steadily and water 3 times if the spring stays dry. After wheat harvest I will hurry in with summer maize on the same 3 mu and keep fertilizer a little heavier because maize answers to it fast when there is water. Cotton I will not make too big because it needs more watching and picking, and some people in the family work outside. Watermelon I will keep on 2 mu only, manage it cleaner, use more potash, and protect it on time because if disease gets in, that crop can fall apart quickly. I watch what nearby farmers do too. Around here, nobody wants to risk an empty field, so I will stay close to the local habit but keep the rates tidy and practical.
